ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ABCD$, $E$ is a point on side $BC$. Taking $AE$ as a side, square $AEFG$ is constructed. If $\angle BAE = 40^\circ$ and $\angle CEF = 15^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that square $AEFG$,\\
it follows that $\angle AEF=90^\circ$,\\
given $\angle BAE=40^\circ$, $\angle CEF=15^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle AEC=\angle AEF+\angle CEF=\angle BAE+\angle B$, which means $90^\circ+15^\circ=40^\circ+\angle B$,\\
so, $\angle B=65^\circ$,\\
given parallelogram $ABCD$,\\
it follows that $\angle D=\angle B=\boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that square $AEFG$,\\ it follows that $\angle AEF=90^\circ$,\\ given $\angle BAE=40^\circ$, $\angle CEF=15^\circ$,\\ thus, $\angle AEC=\angle AEF+\angle CEF=\angle BAE+\angle B$, which means $90^\circ+15^\circ=40^\circ+\angle B$,\\ so, $\angle B=65^\circ$,\\ given parallelogram $ABCD$,\\ it follows that $\angle D=\angle B=\boxed{65^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
In the image, ABCD is drawn as a parallelogram, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right, and E is located on the bottom side BC. With AE as a side, square AEFG is constructed; in the diagram EF is drawn from E toward the upper right, located inside the angle from EA turning to EC; the marked conditions are ∠BAE=40° and ∠CEF=15°.

Because AEFG is a square, ∠AEF=90°. Also because EF is inside ∠AEC, and ∠CEF=∠FEC=15°, ∠AEC=∠AEF+∠FEC=90°+15°=105°. Since the three points B, E, C are collinear, EB and EC are rays in opposite directions, therefore ∠AEB=180°−105°=75°. In triangle ABE, ∠BAE=40°, so ∠ABE=180°−40°−75°=65°. Also because E is on BC, ∠ABE is the parallelogram's ∠B. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, therefore ∠D=∠B=65°.
